newsitem.title: UK: British Airways to buy $1 billion in Boeing planes.
newsitem.headline: British Airways to buy $1 billion in Boeing planes.

text.p: Boeing Co. said Friday that British Airways Plc confirmed an additional order for five more B-777 and three more B-767 wide-body twinjets in a deal worth around $1 billion.
British Airways said the order would increase its fleet of B-777s to 23 over the next two years, with the 767 fleet increasing to 28 aircraft.
The airline said the 777s would mostly be used at Gatwick airport, where BA has been expanding to create a second hub airport for London.

BA said the expansion disproved employee fears that plans to sell off the airline's catering arm at London's Heathrow airport would be followed by similar cutbacks in employment across the company. Staff have threated job sanctions by cabin crew and ground staff.
"These orders are further evidence of our firm intention to stay ahead and grow in this highly competitive business," Chief Executive Robert Ayling said in a statement.

Ayling has said 5,000 jobs out of a work force of about 58,000 are due to go under his Efficiency Programme, through outsourcing and job cuts, to help cut a billion pounds ($1.65 billion) off annual costs by the year 2000.

But a similar number of new jobs are due to be created in core operations. "With this capacity growth we will need more employees, particularly in customer service and flight crew areas," Ayling said.
"We are currently recruiting 5,000 new employees on top of the 3,000 we recruited last year.

He dismissed union allegations that the airline was planning eventually to split off all of its operations to low-cost operators, leaving it to operate as little more than a marketing operation for a brand.
"We will employ more people at the end of the decade, which is why any suggestion that we may in some way be destined to fly as a 'virtual airline' is fear-mongering rubbish," Ayling said.
